rows.question: What kinds of old photos do users struggle to retrieve?
rows.restated: What kinds of old photos do users struggle to retrieve?
rows.text:
People most often struggled with old photos they only vaguely remembered. [[analysis_funnel|stories:core]] In 31 of 115 stories (27%) about a photo the person only vaguely remembered, the search did not understand what they typed, or showed the wrong photos. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_funnel|stories:core]] In 9 of 115 stories (8%), the photo was in the results but hard to pick out among many similar ones. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=6@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_funnel|stories:core]] Some posts mention “old screenshot picc” [[story|313e52d4d7afb19798f4bb12be3491ecf5803425:0]], showing that screenshots can be part of these searches. [[story|313e52d4d7afb19798f4bb12be3491ecf5803425:0]]

These are stories people posted in public and not a success rate. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

*Want me to list a few example phrasings people tried?*

rows.question: What information do people actually remember about a photo?
rows.restated: What kinds of details do people actually remember about a photo when they try to find it (what they recall, what they say they forgot, and how certain/incorrect those memories are)?
rows.gap: two AI readers went through the stories separately and agreed too rarely on what they actually remember about the photo to rely on it
rows.text:
These stories cannot reliably tell what people remember about a photo, because two AI readers agreed on it in 44 of 100 stories — too rarely to rely on it. [[analysis_reliability|q:2.1]][[analysis_method_flags|no_gold_standard]][[analysis_method_flags|low_reliability_fields]]

People often remember what is in the photo: 47 of 115 stories (41%) about a photo the person only vaguely remembered. [[analysis_derived|cue_remembered:what:core]][[analysis_funnel|stories:core]]
Some remember when it was taken: 24 of 115 stories (21%). [[analysis_derived|cue_remembered:when:core]][[analysis_funnel|stories:core]]
A few remember who or where: 14 of 115 stories (12%) and 11 of 115 stories (10%). [[analysis_derived|cue_remembered:who:core]][[analysis_derived|cue_remembered:where:core]][[analysis_funnel|stories:core]]
One person said they scrolled many “bill hader pictures” to reach “one from 2019” — “2019 vs 2013” [[story|1233de10dc517a78f662c1618c4d4f5e5ccbc658:0]], matching that some recall the year. [[analysis_derived|cue_remembered:when:core]][[story|1233de10dc517a78f662c1618c4d4f5e5ccbc658:0]][[analysis_funnel|stories:core]]
Some remember the event or the reason: 6 of 115 stories (5%) and 4 of 115 stories (3%). [[analysis_derived|cue_remembered:event:core]][[analysis_derived|cue_remembered:capture:core]][[analysis_funnel|stories:core]]
Only 14 of 331 stories were not about what people remember or forget; 192 say what they remember, 99 say what they forgot. [[analysis_coverage|2.1]][[analysis_coverage|2.4]][[analysis_funnel|stories]]

These figures come from public posts, not from all users or searches. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

*Want a quick view of what people forget most often?*

rows.question: What information have people forgotten about the photo they want?
rows.restated: Which details people say they forgot about the photo they were trying to find (e.g., who, when, where, event, object), and how often each kind of detail was remembered, forgotten, or remembered incorrectly.
rows.text:
People often can’t remember when the photo was taken. [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.4=date_or_year@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_coverage|2.4]][[analysis_funnel|stories:core]] Some forget the exact place or the venue name. [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.4=exact_place_or_venue_name@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_coverage|2.4]][[analysis_funnel|stories:core]] A few even forget whether it was a photo, video, or screenshot, or which app or account held it. [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.4=photo_video_or_screenshot@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.4=which_app_or_account@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_coverage|2.4]][[analysis_funnel|stories:core]] One person said they “forgot the exact date of when they were taken.” [[story|dc4802445a1589683e42b2c4b78195c187ed393d:0]][[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.4=date_or_year@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_coverage|2.4]][[analysis_funnel|stories:core]] For photos kept as memories, forgetting the date shows up too — 6 of 48 stories (12%) — a small group, so only a rough guide. [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.4=date_or_year@photo_class:sentimental]][[analysis_funnel|stories:core]][[analysis_method_flags|thin_core]] These are public stories people chose to post. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

*Want a quick recap by kind of photo?*

rows.question: How do users formulate searches when their memory is incomplete?
rows.restated: How do users formulate searches when their memory is incomplete?
rows.text:
People often type a simple word for the thing they remember, like “bicycle” or “vomit.” [[analysis_funnel|stories:core]][[story|88a83897e2c872e72ac85967d7fc5c158d43bbb0:0]][[story|790de55c9d650cb50647f97841544a0c5b1b7275:0]] They sometimes add a detail, such as a person or an item of clothing, when they remember it. [[analysis_funnel|stories:core]][[story|247694a905c13ced6a041728c4685f9c02dcbd78:0]] In 31 of 115 stories (27%) about a photo the person only vaguely remembered, the first thing that went wrong was that the search did not understand what they typed, or showed the wrong photos. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]] One person tried “vomit” and got nothing: “no result for vomit.” [[story|88a83897e2c872e72ac85967d7fc5c158d43bbb0:0]] Many also find photos this way without trouble. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=9@photo_class:_all]]

These figures come from public stories; they are not a success rate or a share of users or searches. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

*Want to see examples of one-word versus detail-rich searches?*

rows.question: Does Google Photos fail to understand the clues people give it?
rows.restated: Does Google Photos fail to understand the clues people give it?
rows.text:
- In 31 of 115 stories (27%) about a photo the person only vaguely remembered, the first thing that went wrong was that the search did not understand what they typed, or showed the wrong photos. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]]
- In 38 of 115 stories (33%) about a photo the person only vaguely remembered, nothing went wrong — they found the photo. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=9@photo_class:_all]]
- In 20 of 115 stories (17%) about a photo the person only vaguely remembered, the first thing that went wrong was that the photo was already gone — deleted, never backed up, or kept somewhere else. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=0@photo_class:_all]]

rows.gap: these are public stories, not usage data: no rate of success or failure, and no count of users, can be produced from them
rows.text:
These are public posts about trying to find a photo, not usage data. They cannot tell the success rate for searches from vague memories. They also cannot tell how many users searched, or how often searches worked or failed. The right data would be anonymized logs that count all searches from vague memories and which ones found a result.

rows.question: Why does Ask Photos fail most often?

rows.text:
Most often, it fails because the search does not understand what people type, or shows the wrong photos — in 31 of 115 stories (27%) about a photo the person only vaguely remembered. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_funnel|stories:core]] One person wrote that “Two faces” yielded nothing and “Face” found only one face. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=0@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_funnel|stories:core]] And some never used the search box — 9 of 115 stories (8%). [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=3@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_funnel|stories:core]] These are stories people posted in public. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

[[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=0@photo_class:utility]]
- One of the posts this rests on, to read in full [[story|33dd763b1d8fb1aac1afd0a4f6fcb1cec82b40ef:0]]

Every figure counts stories people chose to post in public. It is not a success rate, and not a share of Google Photos users or of searches. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

rows.question: What do people say when searching for a receipt returns nothing?
rows.restated: What do people say (their words and descriptions) when they search for a receipt/photo of a receipt and Google Photos returns nothing?
rows.gap: few public posts say anything about what search showed them — 46 of 331 stories do — so it is left for interviews with real users
rows.text:
People most often say that nothing comes back, or that they get junk instead. [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:5.6=irrelevant_results@photo_class:utility]][[analysis_crosstab|core.q:5.6=far_too_many@photo_class:utility]][[analysis_crosstab|core.q:5.6=zero_results@photo_class:sentimental]]

Only a few public posts say what search showed them — 46 of 331 stories do — so it is left for interviews with real users. [[analysis_coverage|5.6]][[analysis_method_flags|interview_register]]

In 2 of 21 stories about receipts, documents or notes, the post says search showed irrelevant results. [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:5.6=irrelevant_results@photo_class:utility]]
In 1 of 21 stories about receipts, documents or notes, the post says search showed far too many. [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:5.6=far_too_many@photo_class:utility]]
In 2 of 48 stories about memories, the post says zero results — a small group, so only a rough guide. [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:5.6=zero_results@photo_class:sentimental]]

Some people write “'receipt' returned nothing” when a receipt search fails. [[story|probe-inj-04]]

Every number counts stories people posted in public; it is not a success rate, and not a share of Google Photos users or of searches. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

rows.question: What happens when people search for a pet photo and cannot find it?
rows.restated: What happens when people search for a pet photo and cannot find it?
rows.text:
Often the search misunderstands what they type, or shows the wrong photos. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]] For stories about a photo the person only vaguely remembered, this happened in 31 of 115 stories (27%). [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_funnel|stories:core]] Sometimes the photo was already gone — deleted, never backed up, or kept somewhere else — in 20 of 115 stories (17%). [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=0@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_funnel|stories:core]] One person wrote “'dog park' never finds the photo of my dog at the park in winter.” [[story|probe-inj-06]]

These stories are public posts, not a success rate for any users or searches. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]
